title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 9
paragraphs: On hearing this, the Greeks consulted with one another, and after much was said, the prevailing opinion was that they should remain there that day and camp on shore, then, after midnight was past, set out to meet the ships sailing around. But afterwards, as no one sailed out to attack them, they waited for the late afternoon and sailed out themselves to attack the barbarians, wanting to test both their manner of fighting and the maneuver of breaking through their line.
